newsitem.title: UK: British Airways staff vote for strike.
newsitem.headline: British Airways staff vote for strike.

text.p: British Airways Plc cabin crew have voted overwhelmingly for strike action in a long-running pay dispute, the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) said on Wednesday.
A T&G statement said 75 percent of the 9,000 members balloted had voted, and of these 73 percent were in favour of strike action. The T&G will decide its next move early next week.

T&G national secretary for aviation, George Ryde, said in the statement: "Given this demonstration of the strength of feeling among BA cabin crew, the T&G will not allow the company the opportunity to reconsider its proposals to impose new terms and conditions, including a revised pay structure, before determining our next move early next week."
"It is time to return to the negotiating table," Ryde said. "Instead, management seems to be directing all its efforts into preparing for a strike, rather than negotiating to avoid one."
A British Airways spokesman, speaking before details of the vote were known, said: "...if that is true, it is disappointing but not surprising."
The spokesman said that if the vote favoured industrial action, British Airways "would be forced to put contingency plans into place". He refused to comment further on those plans.

BA has said it would offer employment to others to replace employees who were on strike. BA would need to be given seven days notice ahead of any action, which must be taken within 24 days of the vote being held.

BA chief executive Bob Ayling wrote to staff this week offering to guarantee that no-one would be worse off under the new deal. A three year guarantee was offered as security on this promise, said Ayling. Talks between the two sides broke down after five months of discussions over how to restructure pay.
